beats.headline: A singer with a worm in her head
beats.text: Manasa, the cobra-headed pop star with the eighth-ranked single in the universe, died long ago; she contracted with the Valtay so that one of their parasites could keep her career going, and it is hotter than ever. On the panel she backs the Valtay's attempt to collect their debt from Borant. Then a pulse meant for Carl and Donut hits the trailer she swapped into, and she is gone. Their entertainment assets bring in more than their technology, Ripper says. Then the Valtay claim a dreadnought has destroyed Prince Stalwart's yacht.

beats.headline: A sponsor Borant cannot refuse
beats.text: The Admin notice arrives while Carl is still picking himself up beside the track: he has been sponsored, and viewers of his feed will now see his sponsor's advertisements. The sponsor is the Valtay Corporation. He answers Donut's question out loud with the name, then switches to chat: not a word about them out loud. Borant hates them; they are the ones trying to invade the Borant system, and they are the reason the show started when it did. Borant probably had no choice. It could mean good loot. It could mean Borant tries harder to get him killed.

beats.headline: Not shapeshifters at all
beats.text: Carl asks about the Valtay while Mordecai is explaining the local shapeshifters, and the answer is that they are not shapeshifters. They are a kind of creature called a Gondii. A Gondii enters a dead body within hours of death and reactivates it, reads its old memories, and can keep it running for centuries. Intellect Hunters do something similar, but their bodies begin to rot almost at once, so they are forever hopping. There is also something called an Infiltrator, which Mordecai calls much more insidious, and does not explain.

beats.headline: A creditor with a seat at the table
beats.text: A corporate system government inside the Syndicate, which is to say a company that is also a country and answers to neither description when it is inconvenient. Its people are parasites in the literal sense, riding the bodies of other races. It holds the Borant Corporation’s debt, and it sends a crawler a neural enhancer, which is the sort of gift that is also a note.

beats.headline: The liaison under the hood
beats.text: Orren, the Syndicate liaison who questions Carl over Loita's death, lets slip that the kua-tin intervened on the crawler's behalf and overruled his recommendation to remove him, and that the mudskippers are not known for recognising threats. If the rumors are correct and his own people take over after the next floor, he hopes they will listen to him. Then his hood slips. The swirling darkness is a face-shaped bowl of liquid, and in it Carl glimpses a worm. A Valtay worm.

beats.headline: An attorney for Borant
beats.text: A last-minute lawsuit tries to stop Carl's portal to the ninth floor, and its sole plaintiff is the Skull Empire. The Valtay, currently at odds with Borant, send an attorney to help Borant anyway, with an argument about Carl himself: he now owns stock in a company based in the Skull Empire, and a taxpayer not in arrears is treated differently, so the case belonged in a different court. It is dismissed. Neither the Valtay nor Borant is fond of the orcs.

beats.headline: Regency to the worms
beats.text: Two messages land the moment the interview ends. The first: a regency change has created a conflict of interest, so the Valtay Corporation is removed as one of Carl's sponsors, effective immediately, and an auction will fill the slot. The second goes to the whole planet. A Syndicate court has declared the Borant Corporation independent of the Borant System Government, which automatically executes an earlier ruling handing the Valtay 51% of the corporation. Borant still runs the crawl, and contracts stand, indentures included. Odette thanks the gods, then tells Carl: too bad it's the Valtay.

beats.headline: Borant's newest partners
beats.text: Seventy hours before the Masquerade, the daily announcement thanks Borant's newest partners, the Valtay Corporation, for the capital and help that let the next floor be finished just in time. That floor was not supposed to exist yet: what was going to be the seventh is now the eighth, with its difficulty raised to match. The Valtay have bought themselves a floor, and the crawlers are advised to stay as long as they can rather than go down early.

beats.headline: The floor that broke
beats.text: Mordecai has the story of the broken seventh floor from Mistress Tiatha, and he puts it on the engineers: they built the level just like the fairytale, and the goat did what the kid in the story took thousands of years to figure out. The Valtay are likely irritated with the Borant designers. The Apothecary and the Plenty probably did well out of providing the means, at the cost of the Valtay and the Syndicate, because the Syndicate pays in advance for the tunnels that carry the livestream, and a skipped floor is not refunded.

beats.headline: The Valtay solution
beats.text: The Valtay representative, a worm in the body that once belonged to the Syndicate Prime Minister's mother, assures the council all is perfectly normal. The solution the council backs is theirs: an extinction event, as fast as possible, because the quarantine lifts when the last crawler dies. Their mercenary guilds are recalled off Earth's surface, and the AI has agreed to let tens of thousands of fully armed mercenaries and the sponsors' private armies into the coming war, spread equally among the eight sponsored teams. Well over 150,000. The goal is every crawler, Carl and the cat first.

beats.headline: How a gondii takes a body
beats.text: Tipid, hit in the shoulder and talking too fast, explains what is inside the mages. A gondii worm can move into any dead form and take it over, memories included, though it takes time to learn what to look for and leaves big gaps at first. The Valtay charter says only the willing, and not every gondii lives on the right side of that law. Tipid has heard rumours of outlaw crews, and in a popular tunnel drama about one they are some of the most expensive mercs in the galaxy, at least on the show. A worm that does not care about its host can hop bodies and overclock them. Tipid rates them above the scree.

beats.headline: The Emperator's bomb
beats.text: The Emperator of the Valtay fleet comes through the tunnel gate carrying a system-busting bomb, apparently waiting for the AI to be distracted. It was not distracted. It says so in the middle of a floor announcement, read aloud by a mudskipper who had no idea the text was coming, and adds that it makes no apologies about where that giant suicide bomb just ended up. It does not say where. A creditor who arrives with a bomb has stopped negotiating.

beats.headline: A royalty clause, and a worm
beats.text: Sydnee Iglacia's publisher is a subsidiary of a Valtay company, and her contract lets them hold her royalties for the whole of her natural life, payable to heirs only on proof of her good moral character. The payments can be accelerated, if she signs a Valtay life contract and lets a worm take her over after death. It is not something she would ever dream of doing. Until her rent tripled, anyway.
